SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a county sketch map, what does the north arrow show? (1 mark)
   A. The number of people
   B. The direction of north
   C. The size of the county
   D. The rainfall

2. What do we call the smaller parts into which a sub-county is divided? (1 mark)
   A. Wards
   B. Oceans
   C. Continents
   D. Plateaus

3. Why should a weather chart be filled in at the same time each day? (1 mark)
   A. So that rain stops
   B. So that the records can be compared fairly
   C. So that the chart looks big
   D. So that the sun rises earlier

4. Which clothing helps drivers to see you on a rainy day? (1 mark)
   A. Dark grey clothes
   B. Black clothes
   C. Bright or reflective clothes
   D. Brown clothes

5. How can you keep safe from the sun in the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Stay in the sun all day
   B. Play in the hottest part of the day
   C. Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   D. Avoid drinking water

6. Why was Fort Jesus built? (1 mark)
   A. To make sugar
   B. To keep cattle
   C. To grow food
   D. To guard the harbour

7. Which of these actions harms a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Learning its story
   B. Sweeping the compound
   C. Picking up litter
   D. Writing on the walls

8. Gede Ruins are near which coastal town? (1 mark)
   A. Nyeri
   B. Watamu
   C. Kisumu
   D. Nakuru

9. Which of these is a service? (1 mark)
   A. Treatment by a nurse
   B. A book
   C. A pair of shoes
   D. A bag of maize

10. Why do health workers depend on farmers? (1 mark)
   A. Farmers keep records
   B. Farmers build hospitals
   C. Farmers make medicine
   D. Farmers grow the food they eat

11. What do traders do for farmers? (1 mark)
   A. Teach their children
   B. Build their houses
   C. Buy their crops and take them to markets
   D. Grow their crops

12. Which is a reason why many people live in towns? (1 mark)
   A. No roads
   B. No schools
   C. No water
   D. Jobs, shops and services

13. In a shaded map, which shade usually shows the most crowded area? (1 mark)
   A. The lightest shade
   B. No shade
   C. White
   D. The darkest shade

14. What is a kiondo? (1 mark)
   A. A basket
   B. A house
   C. A shirt
   D. A drum

15. What is a motto? (1 mark)
   A. A school bell
   B. A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   C. A school bag
   D. A class register

16. On a timeline, which event comes first? (1 mark)
   A. The funniest event
   B. The oldest event
   C. The biggest event
   D. The newest event

17. Which activity earns money from visitors to game parks and beaches? (1 mark)
   A. Tourism
   B. Quarrying
   C. Mining
   D. Fishing

18. What is the raw material for tea? (1 mark)
   A. Sugarcane
   B. Cotton
   C. Fish
   D. Tea leaves

19. What is the raw material for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Wheat
   B. Sugarcane
   C. Tea leaves
   D. Milk

20. Which is an agro-based industry? (1 mark)
   A. A bank
   B. A tea factory
   C. A school
   D. A hotel

21. In an essay on good citizenship, what should the beginning say? (1 mark)
   A. What a good citizen is
   B. A list of foods
   C. A recipe
   D. The weather report

22. Which information should you not share with strangers online? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. Your home address and password
   C. The name of your favourite fruit
   D. A joke

23. What is discrimination? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing
   B. Helping
   C. Treating everyone equally
   D. Treating some people unfairly because of who they are

24. Which is a peace message? (1 mark)
   A. Shout louder
   B. Fight for it
   C. Get back at them
   D. Talk, do not fight

25. What should you do if your candidate loses? (1 mark)
   A. Spread rumours
   B. Refuse to work with the winner
   C. Fight
   D. Accept the results peacefully

26. How many tally marks does a group of five look like? (1 mark)
   A. Six lines
   B. One line
   C. Four lines crossed by one line
   D. Two lines

27. What is a suggestion box used for? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping food
   B. Storing books
   C. Collecting rubbish
   D. Pupils drop ideas and complaints

28. Which quality means telling the truth? (1 mark)
   A. Honesty
   B. Laziness
   C. Anger
   D. Pride

29. Which of these is a national government service? (1 mark)
   A. Pre-primary schools
   B. County markets
   C. Cattle dips
   D. Defence and security

30. Who is the head of a county government? (1 mark)
   A. The Governor
   B. The MCA
   C. The chief
   D. The Speaker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State three reasons why Kenya has county governments. (3 marks)

32. Describe how you would design a safety bib for pupils who walk to school. (4 marks)

33. Draw a compass rose and label the four cardinal points. (3 marks)

34. Describe four steps to develop a good quality such as punctuality. (4 marks)

35. List the five items on the sample agenda for a Children's Government meeting. (5 marks)

36. Explain the meaning of an economic activity and give two examples. (3 marks)

37. Give three ethical practices in managing a school enterprise. (3 marks)

38. Explain how pollution can be reduced in an industry. (3 marks)

39. Explain why a mountain can be a source of water for people living far away. (3 marks)

40. Explain the meaning of a good citizen in school. (2 marks)

41. Give three examples of artefacts and say how each is used. (3 marks)

42. Describe how you would draw a sketch map of your county in five steps. (5 marks)

43. Explain three ways in which a county can benefit when its officers know its size and location well. (3 marks)

44. Give two examples of goods and two examples of services. (4 marks)

45. Give two reasons why some areas are sparsely populated. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The direction of north
   A north arrow shows which way is north so the map can be read correctly.

2. A — Wards
   Sub-counties are divided into wards.

3. B — So that the records can be compared fairly
   Observing at the same time gives fair comparisons.

4. C — Bright or reflective clothes
   Bright and reflective clothes stand out.

5. C — Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   These habits protect us from heat.

6. D — To guard the harbour
   It was built as a stone fort to guard the harbour.

7. D — Writing on the walls
   Writing on old walls spoils them.

8. B — Watamu
   Gede Ruins are near Watamu in Kilifi County.

9. A — Treatment by a nurse
   A service is work done for someone. The others are goods.

10. D — Farmers grow the food they eat
   Everyone needs food, including nurses and doctors.

11. C — Buy their crops and take them to markets
   Traders buy from farmers and sell in towns.

12. D — Jobs, shops and services
   Towns offer work and services.

13. D — The darkest shade
   Dark shades show higher numbers.

14. A — A basket
   The kiondo is a woven basket.

15. B — A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   A motto is a short saying of aims.

16. B — The oldest event
   Timelines run from oldest to newest.

17. A — Tourism
   Tourism serves visitors.

18. D — Tea leaves
   Tea is made from tea leaves.

19. B — Sugarcane
   Sugar is made from sugarcane.

20. B — A tea factory
   Agro-based industries use farm produce.

21. A — What a good citizen is
   The introduction gives the main idea.

22. B — Your home address and password
   Private details must be kept safe.

23. D — Treating some people unfairly because of who they are
   Discrimination is unfair treatment.

24. D — Talk, do not fight
   Talking solves problems peacefully.

25. D — Accept the results peacefully
   Accepting results is part of democracy.

26. C — Four lines crossed by one line
   A group of five has four vertical lines and one crossing them.

27. D — Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   It lets everyone share ideas.

28. A — Honesty
   Honesty is truthfulness.

29. D — Defence and security
   Defence is national.

30. A — The Governor
   The governor leads the county.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: To bring services closer to people, to let people take part in decisions, and to share development fairly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use bright cloth, cut it in a vest shape with a head opening, fix reflective strips across the front and back, and test that it is easy to wear and seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat drawing, 1 mark for N at top, 1 mark for E, S and W correct.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the quality, set a small goal, practise every day, and ask a friend to encourage you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Opening, reading the last minutes, reports from cabinet members, suggestions from classes, and closing remarks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: An economic activity is work done to earn income or produce goods and services. Examples are farming and fishing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Be honest with money and customers, be fair in sharing work and rewards, and care for the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each practice.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Treat waste before releasing it, plant trees, and use clean machines or methods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mountains catch rain. The rain flows into rivers. Rivers carry the water to farms and towns far away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: A good citizen in school follows the rules, respects others and does what is good for the whole school community.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rules/respect, 1 mark for the community idea.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clay pot for cooking or storing water, a basket for carrying items, and a stool for sitting. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct artefact with use.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county outline. Draw the sub-county boundaries. Write the names of the sub-counties. Show the neighbouring counties around the edge. Add a north arrow, a title and a key, then colour it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They can plan roads and health centres to reach people. They can share resources with neighbours. They can plan journeys and services better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Goods: maize and shoes. Services: teaching and nursing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Very little rain and no water, and thick forests, swamps or steep land. Accept game parks or few roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
